thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache eviction rate + continuous-batching latency spike on production (svc=runtime, metric=kv_cache_evictions, 5m avg x10). Error rate increased from 0.2% -> 4.1% across generation endpoints. root_ts=1763418276

maria: ack. paging eng-runtime + eng-sre. I'm oncall. starting triage.

kevin: looking. hypothesis: recent batch-config tweak (PR #4392) increased max_batch_size and enabled aggressive prefix caching which exploded KV memory working set under certain seq-length distributions. seeing large GC/delete churn.

sam: seeing same in infra dashboards. hosts in us-west-2 running out of RSS, OOM kill risk for a few pods last 10m. linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/ab12/runtime-kv?org=prod

ellie: do we know which customers impacted? CS is getting alerts from Acme and Helix. need quick per-customer mitigation if possible.

maria: priority: mitigate customer impact first (per-customer overrides), then stabilize global (canary hotfix), then rollback if needed. kevin — can we push a batch-config hotfix behind a feature flag and target canary + specific tenants?

kevin: yes. I can flip a flag to reduce max_batch_size and lower prefix cache TTL. plan: 1) push feature-flag hotfix (canary 5%) 2) add per-tenant override for Acme/Helix immediate 3) monitor 15m, expand to 50% if stable.

kevin: config snippet i'll push (pseudocode):

```json
{
  "flag": "batch_config_tunable_v2",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "defaults": {"max_batch_size": 16, "prefix_cache_ttl_ms": 200},
  "overrides": {
    "tenant:acme-inc": {"max_batch_size": 6, "prefix_cache_ttl_ms": 20},
    "tenant:helix": {"max_batch_size": 8, "prefix_cache_ttl_ms": 30}
  }
}
```

kevin: i'll deploy the flag to canary now and apply tenant overrides immediately. this will not require a full service deploy — runtime reads flags from feature-store and applies on next batch window.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout: feature=batch_config_tunable_v2 to canary=5% (hosts: rt-canary-1, rt-canary-2). rollout_id=roll-20260312-07a

sam: watching memory/eviction graphs. initial trend: canary hosts memory footprint down ~28% within 2 mins. error rate on canary decreased from 3.9% -> 0.6%.

ellie: applied tenant overrides for Acme and Helix via feature-store UI (tenant keys: acme-id-91, helix-id-03). CS notified customers: "we're applying a temporary performance configuration to stabilize your traffic".

maria: good. @kevin please confirm what exact metric we want to be green before expanding. suggest: 5m avg error rate <0.5% and 99th percentile gen latency <350ms for canary.

kevin: agreed. also watch kv_cache_evictions and kv_cache_hit_ratio. I'll start health probes: `curl -s http://rt-canary-1/health` every 30s.

incident-bot: Canary rollout successful to 5% (rollout_id=roll-20260312-07a). Observability checks: PASS (latency drop on canary), anomaly detector disabled for canary hosts.

sam: still seeing a small cluster of non-canary hosts with high eviction spikes — likely where larger sequence-length requests are hitting. per-tenant override should protect those tenants.

kevin: manually forced override for tenant:acme-id-91 applied at 1763418550. config pushed to feature-store, runtime acknowledged: `flag=batch_config_tunable_v2 override applied tenant=acme-id-91`.

ellie: Acme CS confirms reduced errors on their end. "latency is back to normal", will monitor.

maria: handing off to next oncall in 25m. @sam take follow-up monitoring, @kevin keep the flag canary at 5% for 30 mins then prepare a 50% expansion if stable. I'll create an incident ticket with impact numbers and start a follow-up postmortem.

kevin: noted. starting scripted expansion to 50% if canary stays green. expansion plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 10m windows. rollback path: disable flag or revert to batch_config_tunable_v1 (instant).

sam: quick log snippet from affected host:
```
[rt-worker-12] kv_cache: entries=1.2M, evictions/s=4200, mem_rss=7.8G, process_pauses=3
[rt-worker-12] epoch_gc: reclaimed=600k entries, reclaim_latency_ms=120
```

kevin: those numbers match reproduced load tests with long seqs; new config reduces batching so KV working set is smaller and GC evictions fall.

incident-bot: Note: customer impact summary to add to ticket: Acme (high traffic) saw 6-12% client errors for 10-25m window; Helix saw spikes but lower volume. Overall platform error increase peaked at 4.1%.

maria: assigning postmortem owner: @kevin. action items: (1) revert aggressive prefix-caching change in PR #4392 pending deeper root cause, (2) add automatic per-tenant throttles when eviction rate > threshold, (3) add canary-suite with long-seq synthetic load. I'll put these into the incident ticket.

ellie: I'll follow up with affected customers with timeline and remediation steps.

kevin: creating follow-up runbook entry: how to apply per-tenant overrides + safe expansion playbook. saving config templates to infra repo.

maria: handing off now to @sam for overnight watch. keep me posted if anything regresses. thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 

sam: ack, I'll keep the dashboard on and escalate if any metric crosses predefined thresholds.

kevin: will open PR to revert caching change and include load test that reproduces the regression.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. next update in 30m or on change.
